Note values and beaming.back: Beam within the beat, not across it
Note values and beaming.extra: Which is why six quavers beam as three pairs in 4/4 and as two threes in 6/8.

Note values and beaming.back: Adds half the note's value, then half again — a double-dotted crotchet is one and three quarters

Simple and compound metre.back: Simple: each beat divides into two. Compound: each beat divides into three.

Simple and compound metre.front: What the top number means in compound metre
Simple and compound metre.back: The number of divisions, not beats — 6/8 is two dotted-crotchet beats

Simple and compound metre.extra: The C sign means 4/4. Neither abbreviates an English word.

Irregular metres and tuplets.back: Two notes in the time of three — a compound-metre tuplet
"Nice cup of tea" — the words land on the right notes

Rests, and how silence is written.back: The whole rest hangs below the fourth line; the half rest sits on the third
Written as a semibreve rest whatever the time signature
Two slanted lines — a break in the sound, taking time from outside the beat
Same pitch: a tie, adding the durations. Different pitches: a slur, meaning legato.

Expression marks, and the terms.back: French: bring out, to the fore
Go straight on to the next movement, without a break

Reading a printed edition.back: An editorial addition, not the composer's
Reading a printed edition.extra: Dashed slurs mean the same thing.

Reading a printed edition.back: An alternative passage printed on a small stave, usually easier

Intervals, properly.back: The unison, fourth, fifth and octave
Intervals, properly.extra: Seconds, thirds, sixths and sevenths are major or minor instead.

Intervals, properly.back: Count letter names for the number, then compare with the major scale of the lower note for the quality
Both are six semitones. The augmented fourth resolves outward; the diminished fifth inward.

Inversion and compound intervals.back: The numbers add to nine and the quality flips — perfect stays perfect
Larger than an octave: subtract seven for the simple equivalent
Inversion and compound intervals.extra: A major tenth is a major third plus an octave.

All twelve major keys.front: How many key signatures there are
All twelve major keys.back: Fifteen, for twelve keys — B/C♭, F♯/G♭ and C♯/D♭ are enharmonic pairs

The three minors, written.front: What a minor key signature describes
The three minors, written.back: The natural minor only — the relative major's signature
The three minors, written.extra: So harmonic and melodic minors need accidentals written in the music.

Other scales.back: Alternating tone and semitone, eight notes — and only three exist
Japanese pentatonic, 1 2 4 5 6 — bright; folk song and much anime melody
Japanese pentatonic, 1 ♭2 4 5 ♭6 — darker, with semitones. Also miyako-bushi.
Flattened 2nd and 5th — B to B on white keys. Unusable in practice.

Writing a scale, and why spelling matter.back: A seven-note scale uses each letter name once, with whatever accidentals that needs
Writing a scale, and why spelling matter.extra: Which is why double sharps and double flats exist.

Seventh chords and figures.extra: All of them intervals above the bass.
Which is why V⁴₂ goes to I⁶ rather than to root-position I.

Figured bass.back: A root-position triad on that bass note
Applies to the third above the bass
A suspension: play the first interval, then resolve to the second

Roman numeral analysis.back: V/V — "five of five", the dominant of the dominant
Roman numeral analysis.extra: The chord after it is usually the one named after the slash.

Roman numeral analysis.back: A secondary dominant and its target tonicises briefly; a new key confirmed by its own cadence is a modulation

Non-chord tones.back: Held over from the previous chord, dissonant on the strong beat, resolving down by step
Like a suspension, but resolving upwards by step
Approached by step, left by a leap in the opposite direction
The next chord's note, arriving early
Both approached by step — the passing tone continues, the neighbour returns

Cadences in detail.back: PAC: V–I, both root position, tonic in the top voice. IAC: V–I with an inversion, or without the tonic on top.
iv⁶ to V in a minor key, the bass falling by semitone
I⁶₄–V–I — the second inversion tonic delaying the dominant. The standard Classical cadence formula.

The chromatic chords, catalogued.back: Italian A♭ C F♯ · French A♭ C D F♯ · German A♭ C E♭ F♯ (in C minor)
The chromatic chords, catalogued.extra: The German one is spelled like a dominant seventh, which is the enharmonic pivot.

The chromatic chords, catalogued.back: Chords a third away with an altered quality — in C: E, A♭, E♭ major
The chromatic chords, catalogued.extra: No functional relationship. The cinematic lift.

Four-part writing: the frame.back: Root position: double the root · first inversion: root or fifth · second inversion: the fifth · never the leading note
No more than an octave between adjacent upper voices; the tenor-bass gap may be wider

The motions, and the forbidden parallels.front: Why parallel fifths and octaves are avoided
The motions, and the forbidden parallels.back: The two voices fuse into one sound, which defeats a four-voice texture
The motions, and the forbidden parallels.extra: A style rule, not a law — Debussy and rock music use them deliberately.

Species counterpoint.back: 1: note against note · 2: two against one · 3: four against one · 4: suspensions · 5: florid

Imitation, canon and fugue.back: Strict imitation maintained throughout — the second voice follows the first for the whole piece
Fugal entries overlapping more closely than before
Two lines written so that either can be on top
Subject, answer a fifth higher, exposition, episodes, middle entries in other keys, often a stretto and a dominant pedal, then a final statement

Phrase structure, named.back: A period is two phrases, the first ending weakly. A sentence is a two-bar idea stated and repeated, then a continuation and cadence.
One phrase's last bar also being the next phrase's first — which is why bar counts sometimes refuse to add up

The standard forms.back: ABACA — a recurring refrain with contrasting episodes

The standard forms.extra: A suite is a set of dances in one key instead.

Score reading.front: Order of instruments in a score
Score reading.back: Woodwind, brass, percussion, soloists or voices, then strings — highest first within each family

Transposing instruments.back: Sounds a major second below the written note
Sounds a perfect fifth below the written note
Sounds a major sixth below the written note

Reducing a score to two hands.front: What to keep when reducing a score
Reducing a score to two hands.back: The bass line first, then the melody wherever it is, then compact harmony — and leave out the octave doublings

The overtone series.back: C, C, G, C, E, G — an octave, a fifth, an octave, a major third, a fifth
The overtone series.extra: Partials 4, 5 and 6 are a major triad. The chord is in the physics.

The overtone series.back: Octave 2:1, fifth 3:2, fourth 4:3, major third 5:4 — simpler ratios share more partials
They fall between the keys of our scale — noticeably flat of B♭ and between F and F♯

Temperament and tuning.back: Twelve pure fifths overshoot seven octaves by about a quarter of a semitone — which is why every tuning is a compromise
Twelve exactly equal semitones: every key equally usable and equally slightly impure
Temperament and tuning.extra: Fifths very slightly narrow, major thirds noticeably wide of pure.

Temperament and tuning.back: Meantone narrows the fifths for good thirds and leaves a wolf interval. A well temperament spreads the error so every key works, with the common keys better.
That a well-tempered instrument can play in all twenty-four keys
Temperament and tuning.extra: Well temperament rather than equal, as far as the scholarship goes.

Temperament and tuning.back: Tuners deliberately tune the extremes slightly wide, because piano strings' overtones are not perfectly harmonic
Modern standard pitch is A440; Baroque pitch was commonly around A415, about a semitone lower
